explosion.title: Each loan multiplies the states
explosion.caption: Distinct states from TLC, at most one lost reply per run, on a log scale, so equal steps to the right mean equal multiples. Each loan pushes every bar right: with three workers it multiplies the count by 15, then 11, then 9.5, close to the ×10 ticks.

counter.title: A queue that never drains
counter.caption: Each level of the search is one column. With a bound, the columns rise and fall to nothing: the queue empties. With an unbounded counter they settle at about 5,000 and never stop, because every lap of the retry loop is a new state.

symmetry.title: Six names, one state
symmetry.caption: Renaming the workers never changes what can happen, so the checker keeps one state for all six names. Over workers and loans together, that turns 261,673 states into 968.

constraint.title: What a constraint cuts
constraint.caption: TLC builds the states just past the line and checks the invariant on them, then stops. Everything after them, including a bank that loses every reply forever, is never looked at, and the output only hints at it through the generated count.

small-scope.title: One step past the edge
small-scope.caption: The budget stops the search one step before the bug, and the run then looks exactly like a pass. Beside it, a bigger desk finds the same three-step bug, just after more states.
